solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Evidence of a burglar? Disturbing — isn't proof about time?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the time piece
disturbing things moves them about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective muses that the evidence for a break-in is shaky, given doubts over timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' makes FOOPRINS, which 'about' wraps round the time abbreviation; the burglar picture makes the definition a playful example.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks left on the floor by shoes are classic traces a housebreaker leaves behind, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Truth from a Conservative framed by newspaper

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded, so the newspaper's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A Tory claim is presented as gospel by a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something true, so truth works as a synonym in the singular sense.

clue.text: Running ordinary exercise class

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a rating is a classification or grade

explanation.surface: Someone describes a routine gym session that is currently going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is running is functioning, synonymous with being in operation.

clue.text: There's no male inside to spoil what you're reading?

indicators.note: no, combined with inside, says a letter from within the word is to be absent
inside places the missing letter within the word rather than at an end

parts.note: to pamper someone is to spoil or indulge them

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that a household without a man has nothing to indulge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no ... inside' takes M out of the middle of PAMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is what a reader holds while reading, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Huge semi demolished with blokes inside

indicators.note: inside places the men within the scrambled letters
a demolished house is knocked to pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; in Britain a semi is a semi-detached house
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: A big semi-detached house is knocked down with workmen still in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' gives the scrambled I-S-E letters with 'inside' placing blokes after the first two. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense and huge are straightforward synonyms for something of very great size.

clue.text: Tenor and composer on small tours

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A tenor singer and a composer go on short concert tours.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to journey around, so tours as a verb matches in the third person.

clue.text: Sucker taking in old TV serial

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a sap is a gullible person, a sucker

explanation.surface: A dupe gets drawn into a vintage television show.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-running TV dramas are called soap operas, shortened to the same word.

clue.text: Where penguin might be waiting?

parts.note: a penguin stands on frozen ground literally, while the idiom for something held in reserve or put on hold is the same phrase

explanation.surface: A question about where a penguin would stand while it waits.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for postponed or held in reserve also describes literally standing on frozen water.

clue.text: Fresh plants lay around middle of bed, in an attractive manner

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the central piece
fresh signals a new arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: middle of picks the centre letter of the word bed

explanation.surface: Someone sets fresh plants about a flower bed so it looks attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' makes PLASANTLY and 'around' places the centre letter of bed inside it; 'bed' reads as a flower bed in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantly means in an agreeable or attractive way, so the adverbial phrase matches.

clue.text: Vulgar man squeezing female's rear

indicators.note: squeezing means pressing something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man

indicators.note: rear means the back letter of the word female

explanation.surface: A crude man grabs a woman's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' puts E, the 'rear' of female, inside CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap can mean tawdry or in poor taste, a synonym of vulgar.

clue.text: Nasty trick, inhaling hydrogen at the same time

parts.note: mean can mean nasty or unkind

indicators.note: inhaling means drawing in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A spiteful prank involves someone breathing in a gas simultaneously.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means during the same period, so it substitutes for the adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Gust that hurt soprano's eyes

parts.note: a gust is a blast of wind
ow is the cry meaning that hurt
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A blast of wind stings a singer's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are often called the windows of the soul, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Scottish island, for example, backing position

parts.note: Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so these letters are read the other way

explanation.surface: A Scottish island serves as an instance of a supporting stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives GE at the end. 'position' is a verb here, not a noun as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to position them, both verbs meaning put in order.

clue.text: Spotted returning without daughter's requirements

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the reversed word wraps round the other piece
returning means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: seen means spotted or noticed
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter's necessities were noticed on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SEEN into NEES, and 'without' puts it around D. 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are things necessary, a direct synonym of requirements in the plural.

clue.text: Erasing writing quickly

definitions.meaning: crossing out or scraping away writing removes it
scrawling hastily with a pen makes a scraping sound across the page

explanation.definitionFit: Scratching out words erases them, while scratching a note is jotting it hurriedly.

clue.text: Merchant initially abandoned mince he's prepared for restaurant

indicators.note: prepared, as food is, signals the letters being worked into a new order
abandoned means left behind, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word Merchant

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A trader gives up on the minced meat a cook has made for a diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes M (Merchant 'initially') from MINCE, leaving INCE; 'prepared' shuffles INCE HES.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese is British slang for a Chinese restaurant or takeaway meal, an informal shortening.

clue.text: Was present left to absorb son?

indicators.note: to absorb means taking something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: exited means left or went out

explanation.surface: Someone departed to take in a boy, but were they really there?
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be present in reality, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: He's not upset about runs to get trim

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece
upset means knocked over, signalling a rearrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A man is calm about doing some running to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HESNOT into SHOTEN and 'about' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something is to cut it down, the same as making it less long.

clue.text: Specialised new ICT can help after loss of power

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: after loss of means the word help drops a letter

parts.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Fresh computer studies lessons can be useful even after a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after loss of' drops P from HELP leaving HEL; 'new' shuffles ICT CAN HEL. ICT is British school shorthand for information and communication technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical language is specialised to a field, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: After treatment I rang her, having left hospital more annoyed

indicators.note: after treatment, as by a doctor, signals the letters being reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: having left means a letter has gone from the word her

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once discharged from hospital and treated, the patient phoned a woman, who was crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' strips the hospital letter, leaving ER; 'After treatment' then shuffles the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, meaning more cross or annoyed.

clue.text: Succeed by record length in running competition

indicators.note: in places the record and length inside the competition

parts.note: a race is a running competition
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A runner wins a race by a record margin.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to follow and take their place, which is what replace means.

clue.text: Oliver, perhaps, making outrageous claim about America

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters surround the other piece
outrageous means wildly unacceptable, signalling a scrambling of these letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Oliver makes a shocking assertion about the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' makes MICAL and 'about' puts it round the America abbreviation. 'Oliver' looks like a person; it is the Lionel Bart stage show Oliver!
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver! is a famous stage show with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Arms and legs with marks — evidence of a fire?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the former German currency
embers are the glowing remains left by a fire

explanation.surface: Limbs bear scars that suggest someone has been burned.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs of the body are called members, an old but standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Table talk about queen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk piece goes round the queen

parts.note: chat means talk
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Conversation at the dinner table turns to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart is a table of data, the two nouns sharing that sense.

clue.text: Let in first man without hint of any sex appeal

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed from the first man

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible

indicators.note: hint of picks the first letter of the word any

parts.note: it is an old slang term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man first admitted he had none of the allure required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the 'hint of' any, leaving ADM. 'first man' is the Bible's Adam, and IT for sex appeal is dated slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them entry, synonymous with letting them in.

clue.text: Persistently question family for something you can eat

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently for information
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Grilling relatives about something edible.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is an edible gourd, so this vague definition covers it by example.

clue.text: Recognised immediately in outskirts of Kingston

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
outskirts of picks the first and last letters of the word Kingston

parts.note: now means immediately

explanation.surface: Someone is identified straight away on the edge of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' Kingston gives K and N, with NOW between.
explanation.definitionFit: Known means acknowledged or identified, so it substitutes for recognised.

clue.text: Bachelor escapes from eccentric host

indicators.note: escapes from means a letter gets out of the word

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy or eccentric

explanation.surface: An unmarried man flees from a peculiar party-giver.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, especially a military force, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Urgent — I'm to step in

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to mediate is to step in between parties

explanation.surface: Someone announces they must intervene at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means needing prompt action, so it is a synonym of urgent.

clue.text: Ring caught by dog to be found

indicators.note: by means next to, so these pieces sit side by side

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A ring is snatched by a mutt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurs somewhere exists or is met with there, the sense of being found.

clue.text: Those at the game departed, leaving league for good

indicators.note: leaving means that letter goes, to be replaced
for signals the swap, one letter standing in for another

parts.note: late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: Fans quit the match, leaving the league for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving ... for' swaps the L of LATE for G.
explanation.definitionFit: The gate is the attendance at a sports match, the crowd who came in.

clue.text: Without resistance, Noel's play's rewritten for my part

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rewritten letters go round the other piece
rewritten means put down afresh, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A playwright's work is revised so that it no longer meets opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' makes PESONALLY, and 'Without' puts it round the resistance symbol. 'Without' seems to mean lacking; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Personally means as far as I am concerned, an idiom equivalent to for my part.
